surface_forms: sa cousine qui aimait tant la musique

appraisal_events.evidence: « la prééminence du salon Saint-Euverte n’existait que pour ceux dont la vie mondaine consiste seulement à lire le compte rendu des matinées et soirées » ; « ils s’imaginassent volontiers le salon Saint-Euverte comme le premier de Paris, alors qu’il était un des derniers » ; « De tels salons, moins recherchés que fuis, et où on va pour ainsi dire en service commandé » ; she comes the night before « adresser un suprême appel à ses troupes » and each guest attends « à la suite d’implorations, de politesses, de services, et en ayant le sentiment d’honorer infiniment Mme de Saint-Euverte ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator systematically dismantles Mme de Saint-Euverte's apparent eminence, showing that her salon's rank exists only for newspaper readers, that her guests come out of duty while feeling they confer an honour, and that she must canvass for attendance in advance. The same movement includes her purge of the socially obscure, which strands and then excludes Mme de Cambremer.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Nous avancions entre une double haie d’invités, lesquels, sachant qu’ils ne connaîtraient jamais “Oriane”, voulaient au moins, comme une curiosité, la montrer à leur femme » ; « il ne s’en fallait pas de beaucoup pour qu’ils fussent montés sur des chaises, pour mieux voir, comme à la revue du 14 juillet ou au Grand Prix » ; she keeps her gaze « dans le vague, afin d’éviter les gens avec qui elle ne tenait pas à entrer en relations », and disposes of her cousin's palace with « je préférais mille fois son humble trou… Comme camomille, c’est insuffisant. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The duchesse is staged as an unapproachable celebrity walking a corridor of spectators who will never know her, and she exercises that position by screening out unwanted acquaintances and by talking with easy wit; the narrator, walking at her side, is her singled-out companion. The elevation is real even though the gawkers themselves are mocked.

status_effects.explanation: Her standing is decisively lowered: the passage rules that her celebrated salon is in fact one of the last in Paris, sustained by publicity and by guests who attend under compulsion rather than desire.

She is shown soliciting — reviewing her troops, heaping politenesses, imploring attendance — so she acts from a position of asking rather than of granting; the duchesse's remark that she cannot miss a party and would ride a cart to reach one caps the loss of poise.
Left among strangers, feeling she is in the way, she is dropped from the following year's invitations, and the grudging formula obtained on her behalf is so unpressing that she stays away altogether.
She is treated as a public spectacle of rank — pointed out to wives, worth standing on chairs for — while remaining free to refuse contact with the crowd around her.
She holds the floor with an assured comic performance, praising the palace only to prefer her own humble hole and dispatching Mme de Saint-Euverte in a single stroke.

ambiguities: « la vieille Mme de Cambremer » is not securely resolvable: the age marker and the early-Saint-Euverte era point to the dowager marquise, while the bare surface form matches Mme de Cambremer née Legrandin. The exclusion effect is recorded under the surface-matching entity but may belong to the dowager.
